propositions.text: The Appellant is a Mexican citizen who appealed the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The Appellant XXXX XXXX XXXX (the "Appellant") is a citizen of Mexico who has appealed a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed for reasons set out below.
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out below, the appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant is a Mexican citizen appealing the RPD's rejection; the appeal is dismissed for reasons below.

propositions.text: Appellant fears persecution in Mexico from police and cartels due to his former official role in Cuauhtemoc.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that he fears persecution in Mexico, from the federal and state police as well as the Juarez and Sinaloa cartels.

propositions.text: Appellant was appointed as a XXXX XXXX XXXX in Cuauhtemoc in 2016.
propositions.quote: he was appointed as a XXXX XXXX XXXX in his home city of Cuauhtemoc, in the state of Chihuahua, on XXXX XXXX, 2016.

propositions.text: In 2017, armed violence erupted between two cartels, leading to police casualties and state police takeover.
propositions.quote: in XXXX 2017 a period of armed violence erupted between the two cartels in a turf war over the state upon the entry of the Sinaloa cartel, and that several police officers were killed or injured in the violence.

propositions.text: Federal officer JCJ took operational control of police, stripping municipal chiefs of authority.
propositions.quote: a federal officer, JCJ, who had been seconded to the state police was correspondingly put in charge of all police operations. Though the municipal police chiefs were not dismissed, they were stripped of operational authority by JCJ.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges fear of persecution from police and cartels due to his 2016 police role and 2017 cartel violence in Cuauhtemoc.

propositions.text: In early 2017, JCJ told Appellant about a 'cleansing campaign' using extra-judicial methods.
propositions.quote: at the beginning of XXXX, 2017 he was invited to a meeting with JCJ who told him that he would be carrying out a "cleansing campaign" to get the situation under control.

propositions.text: JCJ gave Appellant choice to cooperate or leave, warning about disappearances.
propositions.quote: The Appellant states the CJC then told him that he had the choice of working with CJC and accepting his methods or to "get out". The Appellant states that he was also warned to watch what he said or did, as CJC could easily make people disappear.

propositions.text: Appellant and others resigned rather than work with JCJ in 2017.
propositions.quote: on XXXX XXXX, 2017, the Appellant, along with XXXX other XXXX XXXX XXXX resigned their posts rather than work with CJC.

propositions.text: JCJ was investigated and detained in 2017 for forced disappearance charges.
propositions.quote: on XXXX XXXX, 2017 the state attorney's office later began a criminal investigation of CJC, and that on XXXX XXXX, 2017 CJC was detained by the prosecutor's office on charges of being complicit in the forced disappearance of a person.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant states JCJ initiated a 'cleansing campaign' in 2017, gave him a choice to cooperate or leave, and was later investigated and detained.

propositions.text: In 2017, Appellant was threatened by armed men who told him to leave; he reported to police.
propositions.quote: on XXXX XXXX, 2017, while driving, he was cut off by a vehicle driven by two armed, masked men... told him to "get the hell out"... He reported this to the police the following day.

propositions.text: Appellant obtained an eTA for Canada but went to Mexico City to stay with sister and work.
propositions.quote: he was able to secure an electronic Travel Authorization ("eTA") for Canada. However, he did not use it, and instead went to Mexico City on XXXX XXXX, 2017, where he stayed with his sister and worked as an XXXX.

propositions.text: In 2018, Appellant returned to Cuauhtemoc but stayed with in-laws, worked as XXXX, and took a temporary course elsewhere.
propositions.quote: in XXXX 2018, he returned to his home city of Cuauhtemoc... stayed with his in-laws and continued working as a XXXX... took on a temporary job XXXX a XXXX specialization course in the city of XXXX XXXX, in the state of Campeche, for a few weeks.

propositions.text: Appellant learned CJC was in Coahuila and appeared to be a XXXX XXXX again.
propositions.quote: he later learned through social media that CJC was now in the state of Coahuila, and had seemingly escaped conviction as he, once again, appeared to be a XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant was threatened in 2017, reported it, obtained Canadian eTA but went to Mexico City, then returned to Cuauhtemoc and learned about JCJ's status.

propositions.text: In 2018, neighbours warned Appellant about suspicious people asking for him at his home.
propositions.quote: In XXXX 2018 his neighbours informed him that different vehicles had come by his house and that "people who did not look to have good intentions were asking about" him.

propositions.text: Appellant stayed at relatives' ranch and obtained a second eTA before traveling to Canada in 2019 to claim asylum.
propositions.quote: He states that he then went to a ranch owned by his relatives that was outside of the city for a few days and also obtained a second eTA for Canada. On XXXX XXXX, 2019 he travelled to Canada, where he made a claim for asylum at the airport.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant's neighbours warned him in 2018, he stayed at relatives' ranch, got a second eTA, and claimed asylum in Canada in 2019.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim as lacking connection to Convention refugee grounds and credibility issues.
propositions.quote: The RPD ultimately rejected the Appellant's claim, holding that as his allegations lacked a connection to any of the Convention refugee grounds... he was not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's allegations lacked credibility due to inconsistencies, omissions, and lack of corroboration.
propositions.quote: It further held that his allegations lacked credibility, as they suffered from inconsistencies and omissions that were not adequately explained, and that he had provided virtually no corroborative evidence.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant did not establish protection need under section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: As a result, it held that he had also not established that he was a person in need of protection pursuant to section 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, (IRPA).

propositions.text: RPD specifically found Appellant was not consistent, had uncorroborated second-hand claims, delay undermined fear, and no ongoing threat.
propositions.quote: a. The Appellant was not a consistent and reliable witness... b. The Appellant's claim... was a second-hand account backed by no corroborative evidence... c. The Appellant's conduct and delay... undermined credibility... d. On a balance of probability, the Appellant would not be subject to s. 97 risk...

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim due to lack of connection to refugee grounds, credibility issues, and no established protection need under IRPA s.97.

propositions.text: Appellant appeals RPD decision, seeks recognition as refugee or protected person, new evidence, and oral hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has appealed the RPD's decision and is now asking that the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) recognize him as a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection under s. 97 of the IRPA. He also seeks to introduce, as new evidence, a letter... and a new Affidavit... and requests an oral hearing, if necessary.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in credibility assessment, including trustworthiness, hearsay rejection, delay interpretation, and country context understanding.
propositions.quote: The Appellant essentially argues that the RPD erred in its assessment of his credibility, and in particular that: a. The RPD erred in holding that he was not a trustworthy witness... b. It was unreasonable for the RPD to have expected... c. The RPD inappropriately rejected as hearsay... d. The Appellant's delay... did not reflect a lack of subjective fear... e. The RPD's findings displayed a rudimentary understanding of the country context...

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant appeals, seeking refugee status, new evidence, oral hearing, and argues RPD erred in credibility and country context assessments.

propositions.text: RAD dismisses appeal and confirms RPD decision that Appellant is not a Convention Refugee or protected person under IRPA.
propositions.quote: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention Refugee nor a person in need of protection, pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(a) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision denying refugee or protected person status.

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard after independent evidence assessment, with some exceptions.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Appeal Division reviews decisions of the RPD on a standard of correctness after conducting an independent assessment of the evidence before it.

propositions.text: RAD may apply deferential standard in certain circumstances; here, correctness standard applies after independent evidence review.
propositions.quote: The exception to this rule is that the RAD may apply a deferential standard in certain circumstances. I have conducted my own independent assessment... I find the appropriate standard in this case to be one of correctness.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness standard after independent evidence assessment, applying correctness here.

propositions.text: Appellant submits new affidavit and letter about police report translation issue to correct RPD's conclusion.
propositions.quote: In support of this appeal, the Appellant proposes the admission of an affidavit... along with a... letter... Both of these documents speak to an issue in the translation of the... police report, which the Appellant claims led the RPD to incorrectly conclude that his testimony contradicted the account in the report.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits new affidavit and letter about police report translation to correct RPD's conclusion.

propositions.text: Under IRPA s.110(4), new evidence must arise after claim rejection or be unavailable or not reasonably expected before rejection.
propositions.quote: Subsection 110(4) of the IRPA sets out that an appellant may only present evidence that arose after the rejection of their claim, or that was not reasonably available, or that they could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented at the time of the rejection.

propositions.text: If s.110(4) met, RAD considers factors from Singh including credibility, relevance, and newness of evidence.
propositions.quote: Where evidence meets the requirements of ss. 110(4), the RAD will then go on to consider the additional factors affirmed by the Federal Court of Appeal in Singh, including the credibility, relevance and newness of the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: IRPA s.110(4) limits new evidence; if met, RAD considers Singh factors of credibility, relevance, and newness.

propositions.text: Both new documents were written after claim rejection and could not reasonably have been presented earlier.
propositions.quote: I find that both documents were written after the rejection of the Appellant's claim, and that the Appellant could not reasonably have been expected to have presented the evidence... before the issuance of the RPD decision.

propositions.text: The new evidence is credible, relevant to claim, and new, contradicting RPD's finding on direction Appellant drove.
propositions.quote: I find that this evidence is credible as to source and circumstance; it proves a fact relevant to the claim... and that this evidence is new, in that it provides a basis to contradict the finding of fact made by the RPD as to the direction the Appellant departed in at that time.

propositions.text: The new evidence does not affect Appellant's credibility or central refugee claim issues; no oral hearing allowed under IRPA s.110(6).
propositions.quote: this evidence does not concern or raise a serious issue with respect to the Appellant's credibility, and nor... is it central to the decision... As a result... an oral hearing cannot be held.

paragraphs.summary: The court admits new evidence as credible and relevant but not central to credibility; denies oral hearing under IRPA s.110(6).

propositions.text: RPD found credibility issues rebutted presumption of truthfulness and Appellant failed to prove risk in Mexico.
propositions.quote: the RPD found that due to a series of credibility issues... the presumption of truthfulness had been rebutted... he had not established in evidence that he would be at risk in Mexico.

propositions.text: Court disagrees with some credibility factors but agrees overall with RPD's credibility and risk findings.
propositions.quote: while I disagree that all of these supposed factors should be held to impugn the credibility... I agree with the RPD's findings... that the Appellant did not establish... a serious possibility of persecution, or that he faces a s. 97 IRPA risk.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found credibility issues and no risk; the court partly disagrees but overall agrees with RPD's findings.

propositions.text: Credibility was determinative; RPD did not err in finding Appellant not credible due to inconsistent and evolving testimony.
propositions.quote: credibility was, accordingly, the determinative issue in this appeal. The RPD did not err in finding that the Appellant's inconsistent and evolving testimony undermined his credibility

paragraphs.summary: Credibility was key; the court finds RPD did not err in finding Appellant's testimony inconsistent and not credible.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in finding inconsistency about direction after car incident, calling it microscopic and due to mistranslation.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues upon appeal that the RPD should not have held that a supposed inconsistency... damaged his credibility. He argues that this finding was microscopic, and... the new evidence... indicates... mistranslation.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD erred in finding inconsistency about direction after car incident, citing mistranslation and microscopic issue.

propositions.text: Court agrees direction issue is microscopic and does not draw negative credibility inference on Appellant for it.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Appellant that the question of the direction that he drove after that incident is a microscopic one... I do not draw a negative credibility inference against the Appellant...

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the direction issue microscopic and does not negatively affect Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant argues differing job descriptions in Mexico City are not inconsistent but reflect terminology differences and memory subjectivity.
propositions.quote: The Appellant now argues that the descriptions of where he worked were not inconsistent, but rather reflected differences in terminology... He also states that his inability to recall the company... meant nothing except... memory is a very subjective thing...

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD's expectation of detailed recall was unreasonable given short employment period.
propositions.quote: he argues that it is unreasonable for the RPD to expect an "encyclopedic" account... and that he had only worked at that company for a very short period of time.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues job description differences reflect terminology and memory issues; says RPD's recall expectations were unreasonable.

propositions.text: Court finds RPD reasonably doubted Appellant's credibility about Mexico City employment and inability to name employer.
propositions.quote: I do not find the RPD erred in finding that this evidence of the Appellant was suspect... I do not find the Appellant's explanation... to be persuasive... I find that this does undermine... the credibility of the Appellant...

propositions.text: Six months employment is not short; forgetting employer's name undermines credibility and calls presence in Mexico City into question.
propositions.quote: six months of employment is not a very short period of time... it is not credible that the Appellant simply cannot remember such basic information... calls into question the Appellant's claims as to his activities, and even presence, in Mexico City.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD reasonably doubted Appellant's credibility about Mexico City employment and presence due to inconsistent testimony.

propositions.text: Appellant gave inconsistent testimony about when he left Cuauhtemoc for Mexico City, with shifting dates and confusion.
propositions.quote: he had given divergent evidence... Initially... "Yes, I was there but only until the end of XXXX"... then stated dates were not precise... confused whether he had filed a report Mid XXXX and then left to Mexico City in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellant gave inconsistent and confused testimony about timing of leaving Cuauhtemoc for Mexico City.

propositions.text: Appellant's explanation for date confusion is unreasonable given context of threats and need to flee quickly.
propositions.quote: he was threatened... reported this... forced to immediately uproot his life... one would expect that he would have a good sense of when all of this occurred... I find that this... undermines his credibility...

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellant's explanation for date confusion unreasonable and undermining credibility given threat context.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant's evidence and testimony evolved suspiciously, undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: the RPD found that the evidence and testimony of the Appellant evolved suspiciously, and it essentially found that his credibility was undermined as a result.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's evidence evolved suspiciously, undermining his credibility.

propositions.text: The Appellant first revealed searches at his sister's home in Mexico City during testimony, not previously disclosed.
propositions.quote: the Appellant then suddenly stated, for the first time, that there was something that he had not yet revealed to the RPD: that people had come looking for him at his sister's home in Mexico City on two occasions.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the Appellant's explanation for not disclosing this earlier as unreasonable and found the new allegations untrue.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected this explanation as unreasonable, noting the sophistication and education level of the Appellant, as well as the fact that he was represented in the matter, and further rejected these new allegations as untrue.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant first revealed searches at his sister's home late and rejected his explanation as unreasonable and untrue.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD imposed an unreasonable requirement to amend his narrative as time passed.
propositions.quote: the Appellant now argues that the RPD "imposed an unreasonable requirement on the Appellant [by expecting him] to amend his narrative as time passed"

propositions.text: The Appellant notes RPD Rules do not mandate amending BOC as new evidence emerges.
propositions.quote: pointing out the RPD Rules do not mandate that an Appellant must amend their BOC as new evidence emerges.

propositions.text: The Appellant states he was well-educated but immigration was not his expertise and he rarely spoke with his consultant.
propositions.quote: while the Appellant was admittedly a well-educated XXXX, immigration was not his area of expertise, Canada is a different jurisdiction, and he was represented by an immigration consultant who he rarely spoke with.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the presumption of truth means RPD cannot arbitrarily doubt his sworn statements.
propositions.quote: given the presumption of truth, the RPD cannot arbitrarily doubt sworn statements made by the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD unreasonably required narrative amendments, notes no mandate to amend BOC, cites limited immigration expertise, and invokes presumption of truth.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err; the Appellant's evidence evolved suspiciously regarding searches at his sister's home.
propositions.quote: The RPD did not err in its findings with respect to this issue, and I find that the evidence of the Appellant did evolve suspiciously with respect to the alleged searches at his sister's home in Mexico City.

propositions.text: The new allegations arose late in the hearing when pressed about Mexico City safety and leaving there.
propositions.quote: these allegations did not arise until late in the hearing, when the Appellant was being pressed as to why Mexico City... was not a safe location and why he had chosen to leave there to return to his home city.

propositions.text: The Appellant affirmed his BOC was complete at hearing outset and did not add new information later.
propositions.quote: at the outset of the hearing the Appellant was specifically asked if his BOC was complete and he specifically affirmed this.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not seek to add information during two months between hearing sessions despite discovering it in mid-2019.
propositions.quote: there was even an additional two months between that initial hearing date... and a second hearing session... and nor did the Appellant seek to add this information during this time either.

propositions.text: The Appellant's claim he did not know he could amend materials is not persuasive.
propositions.quote: the Appellant's claim that he had not known he could amend his materials is not persuasive.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err; the Appellant's evidence evolved suspiciously, he affirmed BOC completeness, did not amend, and his excuse is unpersuasive.

propositions.text: It is unreasonable that the Appellant, a highly educated professional, did not realize the need to include relevant information or seek advice.
propositions.quote: it is not reasonable that he would not have realized that it was necessary to include all of the relevant information... or that he would not have... sought information or advice...

propositions.text: The presumption of truth may be rebutted where reasons exist to doubt testimony, as here.
propositions.quote: there is indeed a presumption of truth... however... that presumption may be rebutted where there are reasons to doubt the truthfulness of that testimony.

propositions.text: The Appellant's testimony evolved suspiciously and on balance of probabilities the allegations are untrue, undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the testimony of the Appellant evolved suspiciously... and... on a balance of probabilities, these allegations are untrue... I draw a negative credibility inference...

propositions.text: These findings are significant as they undermine the foundation of the Appellant's entire claim.
propositions.quote: these findings are significant, as they go to the heart of the Appellant's claim... throws into serious doubt the foundation of the Appellant's entire claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's failure to disclose is unreasonable, his testimony is suspicious and untrue, undermining his credibility and claim foundation.

propositions.text: The RPD found no corroborating evidence for the Appellant's claim that neighbours warned him of suspicious activity and gave it no weight as hearsay.
propositions.quote: the RPD noted that... the Appellant had no corroborating evidence... and that it placed no weight on this evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no corroboration for the Appellant's neighbours' warning claim and gave it no weight as hearsay.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by rejecting evidence solely as hearsay, citing s.170 IRPA allowing flexible evidence rules.
propositions.quote: the Appellant makes a series of arguments... that the RPD erred in law by rejecting that evidence simply because it was hearsay... pursuant to s. 170 of the IRPA... the Board is not bound by any legal and technical rules of evidence.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD gave no other explanation for rejecting the neighbours' warning evidence.
propositions.quote: the RPD did not provide any other explanation for why it was rejecting his evidence with respect to the alleged warning of his neighbours.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues letters or affidavits from neighbours would add nothing beyond his testimony and thus were pointless.
propositions.quote: there would have been no point in his providing letters or affidavits from the neighbours... as there would have been nothing... beyond what it could already test with respect to the Appellant's own testimony.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues evidence should not be rejected solely because it is self-interested or from family or friends.
propositions.quote: evidence should not be rejected solely because it is self interested or from the family or friends of an Appellant.

propositions.text: The Appellant reiterates the presumption of truth applies unless valid reasons to doubt exist.
propositions.quote: under Maldonado, there is a presumption of truth as to the sworn testimony of an Appellant, unless there is a valid reason to doubt their truthfulness.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD erred rejecting hearsay evidence, gave no other reason, letters would add nothing, evidence from family is valid, and presumption of truth applies.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in rejecting the neighbours' warning evidence solely because it was hearsay; hearsay is admissible and considered holistically.
propositions.quote: the RPD erred in rejecting the Appellant's claims... solely because of the stated reason that those claims were hearsay... the Board may admit such evidence... and may consider such evidence holistically.

propositions.text: The court does not reject the neighbours' warning evidence because it is hearsay and does not draw negative credibility inference for that reason.
propositions.quote: I do not reject this evidence because it is hearsay, nor draw a negative credibility inference against the Appellant for that reason.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred rejecting neighbours' warning evidence solely as hearsay and does not reject it or draw negative inference for that reason.

propositions.text: The Appellant provided no corroboration or attempt to secure evidence for neighbours' warning claim and gave unpersuasive explanation.
propositions.quote: the Appellant has indeed provided no corroboration... Nor... had he made any attempt to secure such documentation... I find it unreasonable... and I do not find the Appellant's explanation... persuasive.

propositions.text: The Appellant is sophisticated and well-educated and would understand the importance of corroboration and seeking advice from his representative.
propositions.quote: he is a sophisticated and well-educated party... he would be well aware of the importance of providing corroborating evidence... and... he is... represented... it is not reasonable that he would not have... made inquiries...

propositions.text: The Appellant provided corroborating evidence for other claim facets but not for neighbours' warning.
propositions.quote: he has accordingly provided a great deal of corroborating evidence with respect to the other facets of his claim, if not this one.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant gave no corroboration or effort for neighbours' warning, his explanation is unpersuasive, and he is sophisticated and represented.

propositions.text: Presumption of truth does not excuse failure to provide corroborative evidence, especially with other credibility concerns.
propositions.quote: there is generally a presumption of truthfulness before the Board, this does not excuse a claimant from making a genuine effort to provide corroborative evidence... particularly where other credibility concerns exist.

propositions.text: The Appellant's failure to seek corroboration seriously undermines the credibility of this allegation and his overall credibility.
propositions.quote: the Appellant's failure to even seek corroborating evidence... seriously undermines the credibility of this allegation, as well as that of the Appellant generally.

propositions.text: These findings are significant as they go to the heart of the claim and undermine its foundation.
propositions.quote: these findings are significant, as they, too, go to the heart of the Appellant's claim... throws into serious doubt the foundation of the Appellant's entire claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds presumption of truth does not excuse lack of corroboration, which seriously undermines the allegation and claim foundation.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant's behaviour showed lack of subjective fear, noting delayed use of eTA and returns to threatened city.
propositions.quote: the RPD essentially found that the behaviour of the Appellant demonstrated a lack of subjective fear... he never utilized this to journey to Canada... he returned to his home city... and continued to openly practice XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's behaviour showed lack of subjective fear due to delayed travel and returns to threatened city.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues his actions reflected subjective fear and delay in leaving was a last resort and insurance policy.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that his actions did reflect a subjective fear... he viewed leaving his country as a last resort, and he had only obtained the eTA as an insurance policy.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues his returns and open practice were cautious and incremental, living discretely while maintaining career.
propositions.quote: he had moved from city to city with trepidation... he lived as discretely as possible while maintaining his career.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues his actions showed subjective fear, delay was last resort, and returns were cautious and discreet.

propositions.text: The court accepts the Appellant's explanation that delay in leaving Mexico does not demonstrate lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: I do not find that the Appellant's failure to immediately leave Mexico... can be taken to demonstrate a lack of subjective fear. I accept as reasonable the Appellant's argument...

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts the Appellant's explanation that delay in leaving Mexico does not show lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: The Appellant's return to Cuauhtemoc and open practice indicate lack of subjective fear and undermine credibility.
propositions.quote: I do find that that Appellant's return to Cuauhtemoc and his apparently open practice of XXXX there do indeed indicate a lack of subjective fear... this does further undermine the credibility of his allegations.

propositions.text: The Appellant's explanation for returning after six months is not reasonable given the alleged danger.
propositions.quote: I do not find his explanation for why he would return after a mere six months persuasive.

propositions.text: It is not reasonable he would return to the city of danger, openly practice, and live at original address after returning.
propositions.quote: it is not reasonable that he would choose to return to the very city where the most pronounced danger to him existed... and that he would do so after only six months... openly practice XXXX... move back to his original address.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant's return and open practice show lack of fear, his explanation is unreasonable, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The RPD found no evidence of ongoing existential threat; noted Appellant faced no further threats after initial incidents and complied with warnings.
propositions.quote: the RPD held that it had not been presented with reliable evidence suggesting that the Appellant faced an on-going existential threat to his safety in Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no evidence of ongoing existential threat to the Appellant after initial incidents and compliance with warnings.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD's findings were speculative and failed to consider objective evidence of police targeting and corruption.
propositions.quote: the Appellant argues that the findings of the RPD were speculative and reflect a lack of understanding about how cartels operate in Mexico... failed to consider the objective evidence indicating that police are targeted by cartels for violence, and that police corruption is common.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD's findings were speculative and ignored objective evidence of police targeting and corruption.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not address why CJC would target him given compliance and CJC's arrest and relocation.
propositions.quote: the Appellant essentially does not address the RPD's question as to why CJC would have any interest in him... CJC had been arrested... and was living in another state entirely.

propositions.text: The Appellant presented no evidence contradicting that CJC no longer had ability or motivation to target him.
propositions.quote: the Appellant has presented no evidence to the contrary on either front.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant did not explain why CJC would target him and presented no evidence contradicting CJC's lack of ability or motivation.

propositions.text: The court agrees there is objective evidence of police corruption and cartel influence in Mexico.
propositions.quote: there is plentiful objective evidence indicating that there is significant corruption in the Mexican police forces, and undoubtedly the cartels do wield influence...

propositions.text: The Appellant did not explain or provide evidence linking cartels to his persecution or why cartels would target him.
propositions.quote: the Appellant has not explained why this is or how this is consistent with the core of his claim... has provided no evidence to this effect.

propositions.text: The Appellant's evidence shows he resigned to refuse unlawful acts against cartels and had no interactions with cartels.
propositions.quote: his evidence was that he resigned being the XXXX XXXX, as he refused to take part in CJC's unlawful cleansing campaign against the cartels. He also never presented any evidence as to having had any interactions with the cartels, at all.

propositions.text: The Appellant never linked CJC and cartels or provided evidence of such a link.
propositions.quote: in neither his Appellant's memorandum, nor in his testimony has the Appellant ever spoken to this or of a link between CJC and the cartels... he has provided no evidence to this effect.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds objective evidence of corruption but the Appellant did not link cartels to his persecution or provide evidence of such a link.

propositions.text: The Appellant has not established he is pursued by CJC or the named cartels.
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has not established in evidence that he is being pursued by either CJC or the cartels that he has named.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant has not established he is pursued by CJC or the named cartels.

propositions.text: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant is not credible and his claim is not established on a balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: I agree with the finding of the RPD that the Appellant is not a credible witness... the Appellant's claim is not established.

propositions.text: The Appellant is not subject to risk to life or cruel treatment in Mexico and is not a Convention refugee under IRPA s.96.
propositions.quote: he is not subject to a risk to his life, or of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or torture in Mexico... he is further not a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the RPD that the Appellant is not credible, his claim is not established, and he is not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the appeal is dismissed.

propositions.text: The decision of the RPD is confirmed that the Appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: I confirm the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection within the meaning of s. 96 and s. 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.
